# `kernel/execution/ExecutionHorizonPolicy.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/execution/ExecutionHorizonPolicy.js`

Pure adaptive execution-window policy. It has no authority vocabulary and can only reduce caller-supplied action/concurrency ceilings. Descriptor risk and reversibility dominate calibration: confidence never changes approval, capability, tool selection, or the static execution ceiling. Callers must enforce the returned action and mutation limits as hard dispatch boundaries.

## Classes

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `static select({ descriptors = [], evidence = {}, ceiling = {} } = {})` |  |
| `admit` | `static admit(horizon, { dispatchedActions = 0, dispatchedMutations = 0, readOnly = true } = {})` | Decide whether one more descriptor-authorized action fits inside an already selected horizon. This is deliberately authority-free: it can only reject work after a caller ceiling or mutation-observation boundary has been reached. |

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
